topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutations, clonal evolution and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can lead to cancer when the affected cells and their surroundings permit mutant clones to persist and expand.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer while weighing competing explanations for variation in risk.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to cancer, developing the general mechanisms through the example of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, often through processes that depend on metabolism.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how tumour promoters enable previously initiated cells to grow, using asbestos and experimental skin carcinogenesis to explain the distinction.

topics.label: Biological context of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the mechanistic account by showing that carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context in which an exposure acts.

topics.label: Investigating carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence linking exposures to cancer can be obtained and what limits the conclusions drawn from it.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
